# Plane Design Language v1.3 reference

<!-- GENERATED by schema.docs (plane schema docs) from schema/plane.schema.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Canonical design file. Units are fixed: millimetres, grams, newtons, degrees, seconds. Body frame: origin at the nose datum, +x aft, +y starboard (right), +z up.

## Definitions

### `slug`

Type: string

Pattern: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$`

### `vec3`

Type: array of number

### `component`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `slug` | yes |  |
| `type` | one of `fuselage`, `wing`, `tail_surface`, `boom`, `motor`, `propeller`, `battery`, `esc`, `flight_controller`, `receiver`, `servo`, `payload`, `landing_gear`, `structure`, `pod`, `other` | yes |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `geometry` | `geometry` | yes |  |
| `planform` | object |  | v0.4. Aerodynamic planform of a component whose geometry is not a lifting_surface (e.g. a mesh wing). Used ONLY by tier-3 aero (lift slope, stall, static margin, neutral point). It creates no geometry for collision, mass or export. Not allowed on a component whose geometry is a lifting_surface. |
| `planform.lifting_surface` | `lifting_surface` | yes |  |
| `planform.origin` | `vec3` | yes | Body-frame position of the root leading edge (mm). |
| `planform.rotation_deg` | `vec3` |  | Intrinsic roll, pitch, yaw of the planform about x, y, z (deg). Default [0,0,0]. |
| `position` | `vec3` | yes | Component origin in body frame (mm). For box/cylinder: centre. For lifting_surface: root leading edge. For point_mass (v0.4): the point where the mass sits. |
| `rotation_deg` | `vec3` |  | Intrinsic roll, pitch, yaw about x, y, z (deg). |
| `mass_g` | number |  |  |
| `cg_offset` | `vec3` |  | CG relative to the component's geometric centroid (mm). Default [0,0,0]. |
| `material` | string |  |  |
| `cavities` | array of `cavity` |  | v0.3. Solid box or cylinder shapes subtracted from the component's local mesh before rotation_deg is applied. A cavity may break through the outer surface (an opening). |
| `manufacturing` | object |  |  |
| `manufacturing.method` | one of `laser-cut`, `3d-print-fdm`, `3d-print-sla`, `cnc-router`, `cnc-mill`, `hotwire-foam`, `foamboard`, `composite-layup`, `waterjet`, `hand-cut`, `purchased` | yes |  |
| `manufacturing.machine` | string |  | Optional machine id from standards/manufacturing.yaml |
| `manufacturing.part_number` | string |  | For purchased parts |
| `manufacturing.cost_usd` | number |  |  |
| `provenance` | `provenance` |  |  |
| `propulsion` | object |  | Motors only. |
| `propulsion.max_thrust_n` | any | yes | Peak static thrust, N, from a datasheet or bench test; the text pending when no source exists (checks that need it are skipped). |
| `propulsion.axis` | `vec3` | yes | Direction of the thrust FORCE on the aircraft (unit vector, body frame). Forward thrust is [-1,0,0] for tractors and pushers alike; hover lift at 0 deg pose is [0,0,1]. |
| `propulsion.role` | one of `lift`, `cruise`, `both` |  |  |
| `propulsion.max_current_a` | number |  | peak current at max_thrust_n, from a datasheet or bench test |
| `propulsion.prop_diameter_mm` | number |  |  |
| `propulsion.spin` | one of `cw`, `ccw` |  | PDL 1.1. Sense of rotation of the prop seen from the side the thrust force points to, looking back at the motor (a hover lift motor: seen from above). The reaction torque on the airframe about the thrust axis is the opposite way: a cw prop adds +axis, a ccw prop -axis. |
| `propulsion.torque_per_thrust_m` | number |  | PDL 1.1. Prop reaction torque per unit thrust (N*m per N, a length in metres; measured or from the prop data). Needs spin and torque_per_thrust_m_source. |
| `propulsion.torque_per_thrust_m_source` | string |  | PDL 1.1. Where torque_per_thrust_m comes from (document, test or plant file with its line). |
| `battery` | object |  | PDL 1.0 (D21). Battery components only. |
| `battery.capacity_mah` | number | yes |  |
| `battery.cells_s` | integer | yes |  |
| `battery.max_discharge_c` | number |  |  |
| `mass_model` | one of: `material` / `density_g_cm3` |  | v1.2. Mass computed from the generated geometry: volume x density + extra_g. Use instead of mass_g (giving both is an error). Only for a component whose geometry is a generator. |
| `mass_model.material` | string |  | Id of an entry of the design's materials block or of standards/materials.yaml. |
| `mass_model.density_g_cm3` | number |  |  |
| `mass_model.extra_g` | number |  | Mass not in the volume (glue, tape, hardware), grams. |

### `attachment`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  |  |
| `parent` | `slug` | yes |  |
| `child` | `slug` | yes |  |
| `method` | one of `bolted`, `glued`, `press-fit`, `magnet`, `hinge`, `zip-tie`, `tape`, `printed-integral`, `clamp`, `slot-tab` | yes |  |
| `location` | `vec3` | yes | Joint point in body frame (mm). Must lie on or inside both parts (within tolerance). |
| `embed_ok` | boolean |  | true if the child is meant to pass into the parent (spar into slot, motor into pod). |
| `kinematic_link` | boolean |  | v0.4. true if the child is moved by a linkage the schema does not model (e.g. a servo pushrod driven by an elevon horn). Tier-1 pose and sweep interference skips pairs of this child with a part moved by that pose and reports them as one WARN per pose (T1.kinematic_link). Static (0 deg) checks are unchanged. |
| `hinge_from` | `generator` |  | v1.2, optional. generator = the resolved location, articulation.pivot and articulation.axis come from the child's wing_panel hinge line (part elevon, side left or right) and follow its parameters; the values written here are a placeholder. An aileron, flap or elevon hinge follows a wing change this way. |
| `rated_load_n` | number | yes |  |
| `rating_basis` | one of `sourced`, `derived`, `placeholder` |  | v0.4. Where rated_load_n comes from. sourced: a published or tested capacity. derived: an allowable times measured geometry. placeholder: no capacity in the source; the value is not a capacity, and tier-2 load checks skip this joint (never PASS or FAIL it). |
| `articulation` | object |  | v0.2. The joint moves. Rotation applies to the CHILD side: the child and everything attached downstream of it (reached from the child without crossing back through this joint). 0 deg = the geometry as written. |
| `articulation.type` | one of `revolute`, `continuous` | yes | v1.3: type continuous = spins without limit (a wheel on its axle); no range_deg, no poses. |
| `articulation.pivot` | `vec3` | yes | A point on the rotation axis, body frame (mm), at 0 deg. |
| `articulation.axis` | `vec3` | yes | Rotation axis direction (right-hand rule), body frame, at 0 deg. |
| `articulation.range_deg` | array of number |  | [min, max] angle in degrees. |
| `articulation.poses` | object |  | Named poses -> angle in degrees (each within range_deg). |
| `connection` | string |  | v1.0. Id of a connection type in standards/connection-types.yaml (for example CT-M3-SHCS-INSERT). Optional. T1.interfaces.connection_known fails an id that is not in the library. |
| `seat` | string |  | v1.0. Optional. Short text naming the recess, pocket or slot machined in the parent that receives the child (for example "pod recess cut in the core"). Data only; no check reads it. |

### `relpath`

v1.0. Path relative to the design folder, forward slashes only: no drive letter, no leading slash, no backslash, no .. segment.

Type: string

Pattern: `^(?![A-Za-z]:)(?!/)(?!.*\\)(?!(.*/)?\.\.(/|$)).+$`

| `to_port` | `slug` |  | v1.3. Name of a port in the library part of component `to` (knowledge/parts/<id>/part.yaml ports); the wire ends there. Default: the CG of `to`. |
| `waypoints` | array of `vec3` |  | v1.3. Points (design frame, mm) the wire passes between its ends; [] = straight. Any of from_port, to_port, waypoints makes the harness routed: it is drawn as a tube in Studio and T7 checks the route. |
| `diameter_mm` | number |  | v1.3. Drawn wire diameter, mm (default 1.5). Visual only. |

### `mechanism`

v1.0. A pull-this-moves-that mechanism between attachments.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `slug` | yes |  |
| `driver` | string | yes | Attachment id. |
| `kinematics` | one of `ratio`, `four_bar` |  | v1.3, optional, default ratio. ratio = the follower angle is the declared expect ratio x input (as before). four_bar = the follower angle is solved so that the distance from the link.driver_end point on the arm to the link.follower_end point in the horn stays constant (rod length), and the rod is drawn pinned between them; needs link, exactly one driven attachment and the same attachment in expect; input_range_deg must contain 0. |
| `driven` | array of string | yes |  |
| `input_range_deg` | array of number |  |  |
| `expect` | array of object |  |  |
| `expect[].attachment` | string | yes |  |
| `expect[].ratio` | number | yes |  |
| `link` | object |  | v1.0. The linkage the schema does not otherwise model: the two attachments where it is pinned. driver_end is a kinematic_link attachment on the driver side (e.g. the pushrod on the servo arm); follower_end is an attachment on the side moved by the driven joint (e.g. the clevis pin in the horn). Their `location` points give the lever ratio checked by T6.ratio, and their parts are not counted as colliding with the driver-side linkage part (T6.link). |
| `link.driver_end` | string | yes | Attachment id. |
| `link.follower_end` | string | yes | Attachment id. |
